summary: Martin Joachim Kümmel works in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Freiburg (~1990–1998) under Eva Tichy, Helmut Rix, and others. He held a post at the University of Jena around 2013.

Martin King Whyte is a scholar of Sinology and other fields. He studied at Cornell University (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1966–1971). His career includes positions at the University of Michigan (~1970–1994) and Harvard University (~2000).

Martin Lehnert specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and was attested in 2016 as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Martin Lowenthal works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu, and held posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1973–1978) and Heidelberg University (~1978–1980), and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1990–2014).
Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg by 2004 under Barend Jan Terwiel and held an attested post at the University of Hamburg in 2004.

Martin T. Adam specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University, where he earned his PhD under Richard P. Hayes (attested 2002), alongside teachers including Kameshwar Nath Mishra.

Martin Willson was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Lambert Schmithausen and earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), where she also held a post.

Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2015) under the supervision of Donald S. Lopez Jr. and mentoring of Ester Bianchi.
Maruo Ujiie is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Tribhuvan University (attested 1970). He held an attested post as a lecturer at Koyasan University in 1970.

Marvin Eisenberg was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a post at the University of Michigan (~1949–1993).

Mary Clabaugh Wright specialized in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Vassar College (~1934–1938) and Radcliffe College/Harvard University (~1938–1951), and held a faculty post at Yale University (~1959–1970).
Mary Jaksch works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey, attested in 2007.

Marybeth White works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a double major honors degree from York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Marylin Martin Rhie specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. She studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1955), held a post at Otani University (~1960–1971), and became professor emeritus at Kyoto University (~1993–2015).

Masaaki Hattori is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Kyoto University (1955, 1961–1988), Osaka Gakuin University (1989), and several international visiting professorships.

Masaaki Nitta is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1969). He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (~1980–1992) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1983–1988).

Masaaki Nohin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He served as an assistant professor (attested 1999–2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.
